def: An agent that operates a graphical interface the way a person does, receiving what is on the screen and emitting mouse and keyboard actions.
A computer-use agent restricted to a web browser, where page structure and accessibility information are available and the environment is easier to sandbox.
The program around the model that captures observations, executes the model's chosen actions on the machine and enforces policy before it does.
Mapping a description such as the Submit button to a precise target on the screen, in pixels or as a reference to an element.
A machine-readable hierarchy of interface elements with roles, names and states, exposed for assistive technology and usable as a compact text observation for agents.
The Document Object Model: the browser's tree of HTML elements for the current page.
Overlaying numbered marks on the interactive regions of a screenshot so the model answers with a mark number instead of estimating coordinates.
The number of physical pixels per coordinate unit on a high-density display, which a harness must account for when converting model coordinates into clicks.
Verifying after an action that the screen shows the state the action should have produced, rather than trusting the harness's report that the event was delivered.
Deterministic code between the model's proposed action and the real mouse and keyboard that allows, requires confirmation for, or denies the action.
A benchmark of 369 computer tasks in real operating systems and applications, scored by execution-based scripts that inspect the resulting state.
